findings.whisperHostDarwinArm64: Retain Python/MLX. Both sherpa Whisper precisions are slower; INT8 exceeds 1 GiB loaded RSS and has 2.55x the Mandarin CER after T2S; FP32 is still slower/larger and does not recover Mandarin quality.
findings.senseVoice: Leading Mandarin candidate: 9.1115% CER after T2S versus MLX 12.0543% (24.4% relative improvement), similar English WER, ~3x faster warm than MLX, and <1 GiB RSS.
findings.productionReplacement: Prior preserve-Whisper conclusion is superseded as a proposal by the accuracy-first expansion. Fun-ASR-Nano GGUF Q8 is now the evidence-leading single Chinese/English/code-switch candidate on macOS arm64. Selection remains pending user approval and a persistent packaged-worker/target proof; no implementation handoff is authorized.
findings.hostArchitecture: Provider packages must own a host appropriate to their selected backend. The public protocol/catalog is host-neutral; Python and Node are both valid provider-private hosts when evidence supports them. No Electron/system-interpreter execution.
findings.minimalMlx: A torchless experimental venv reduced runtime footprint but violates mlx-whisper declared dependency metadata and fresh first import was 25s; it is rejected as a production shortcut.
findings.realMixed: On 30 ASCEND clips/5 speakers in auto mode, SenseVoice led at 22.56% MER and 82.47% embedded-English recall versus MLX 64.48%/65.21% and sherpa Whisper 41.92%/69.32%. SenseVoice materially improves real code-switch speech but still misses the <=15% MER and >=85% recall replacement gates.
findings.explicitZhMixed: For the same real mixed clips in explicit zh mode, SenseVoice achieved 23.98% MER/78.63% recall; both Whisper implementations regressed severely. Auto remains the evidence-supported mixed-language mode; explicit zh must not be claimed to preserve code-switch quality.
findings.packagedMlx: A dependency-consistent, runtime-owned CPython 3.12.13 + MLX provider retained Torch, removed only bytecode/build-install tooling, included the model, required no ffmpeg/system interpreter/live pip, relocated successfully, measured 1,333,502,573 installed file bytes (below 1.25 GiB), and achieved 10-run process-cold p95 1.577 s plus warm p95 148 ms.
findings.nonArm64Feasibility: Pinned CPython 3.12.13 install-only assets exist for macOS x64, Linux x64, and Windows x64, and faster-whisper 1.2.1 binary dependency graphs resolve for Python 3.12 on all three targets. This is packaging feasibility only; target execution/quality/performance remains a publication gate.
findings.accuracyPriorityRevision: The user explicitly made recognition quality the primary decision criterion and stated approximately 10 seconds or more can be acceptable. RSS and latency remain feasibility/operational evidence, not automatic selection precedence.
findings.paraformerLarge: INT8: 10.583% Mandarin CER, 26.627% English WER, 26.643% ASCEND MER/77.26% recall. FP32 changed quality only marginally while increasing model size and RSS; neither is competitive with Fun-ASR or SenseVoice overall.
findings.funAsrNano: Best tested unprompted candidate: 8.546% Mandarin CER, 4.505% English WER, 20.959% ASCEND MER/86.30% embedded-English recall, 11.399% synthetic MER/77.12% broad English recall. First-ever local invocation was 13.48 s; later isolated process-per-request p95 was 1.936 s with 2.077 GB max RSS. Models+candidate binary were 1,281,141,776 bytes.
findings.boundedContextTerms: A provider-private prompt using an exact 15-entry product-term list raised exact scored product phrase recall from 6/13 to 13/13. It caused small real/monolingual regressions and a larger broad synthetic-English recall tradeoff, so context terms must be optional, bounded session configuration with regression gates, not a global hidden prompt.
findings.expandedCandidates: Faster-whisper and whisper.cpp Small are viable runtimes but materially worse for Simplified Mandarin. Stock llama.cpp/Qwen3-ASR 0.6B Q8 is fast and package-feasible but Fun-ASR was 1.079 absolute CER points better on 200 paired clips (95% bootstrap interval 0.348-1.961 points in Fun-ASR favor), and Qwen persistent RSS reached 4,778,541,056 bytes (4.45 GiB) with default prompt caching and 5,529,157,632 bytes (5.15 GiB) with prompt caching disabled.

english.otherTargets: Preserve faster-whisper Small subject to actual target package/non-regression proof

expandedCandidateInvestigation.largerQwenExclusion: Qwen3-ASR 1.7B Q8 decoder plus projector is 2,520,744,288 bytes before the runtime, exceeding the 1.25-GiB per-provider package ceiling; 0.6B BF16 and 1.7B BF16 also exceed it.
